findings.title: Adding abstract order() breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public SPI discovered via ServiceLoader. Adding the abstract method `int order()` (without a body) is a source- and binary-incompatible change for every implementation that lives outside this PR. Any existing implementation (e.g. the copy in the keycloak-client repository that this PR says will be synced later, or a third-party provider jar) that was compiled against the previous interface has no `order()` method, so `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider()` will now throw `AbstractMethodError` when it calls `CryptoProvider::order` on it; recompiling such a provider also fails until it is changed. Providing a `default int order() { return 100; }` would preserve compatibility and let new providers opt into a higher precedence only when needed.

findings.title: Removing the multiple-providers fail-fast allows silent non-deterministic (possibly non-FIPS) selection
findings.body: Previously `detectProvider` threw `IllegalStateException` when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath, forcing an explicit single-provider configuration. The new code only logs the others at debug level and returns `foundProviders.get(0)`. This is dangerous because `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` all return `order() == 200`, so they tie. The `reversed()` sort is stable, so the winner among tied providers is decided by ServiceLoader/classpath order, which is non-deterministic. A misconfigured FIPS or Elytron deployment that accidentally has both the FIPS/Elytron provider and the default BC provider present would previously fail fast; now it may silently pick the non-FIPS `DefaultCryptoProvider` and run with non-FIPS crypto (or pick the wrong provider on EAP). Consider keeping a hard error when multiple providers share the top order, or at minimum logging at warn/error.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JVM default keystore provider, not a BouncyCastle provider
findings.body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is documented by the `CryptoProvider` interface as returning the (non-FIPS or FIPS) BouncyCastle security provider, but this implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which on a stock JVM is the platform provider (e.g. `SUN`). Any caller that relies on the contract — for example code that registers it as the BC provider or uses BouncyCastle-specific behavior — will receive the wrong provider and fail or silently behave differently. If the intent is to have no BC dependency, the method should either be documented/typed accordingly or the provider should be obtained in a way consistent with the contract.

findings.title: ECDSA test only round-trips conversions and uses a default P-256 key for ES384/ES512
findings.body: The test generates a single default `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` key (typically P-256) and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512. It never checks that the reconstructed DER signature actually verifies against the public key, nor that the code handles a curve whose field size matches the algorithm's `getSignatureLength()`. Because `asn1derToConcatenatedRS`/`concatenatedRSToASN1DER` symmetric padding makes the DER→RS→DER→RS round-trip succeed even when `signLength` (66 for ES512) does not match the real 32-byte r/s, the test would pass even if the conversion were wrong for real P-384/P-521 keys. Use a curve matching each algorithm and assert the round-tripped/re-encoded signature verifies against the public key.

findings.title: readSequence silently returns an empty list for indefinite-length encoding
findings.body: `readLength()` returns -1 for the indefinite-length form (0x80), but `readSequence()` uses that value directly in `while (length > 0)`, so an indefinite-length sequence produces an empty list instead of a clear error. A caller that reads it (e.g. `asn1derToConcatenatedRS`) then fails later with the misleading message "Invalid sequence with size different to 2". Since only DER (definite length) is valid here, reject `length == -1` with an explicit error.
